# Manuscript Rules

Write reader-facing Korean Markdown for a beginner-friendly technical book.

## Before Editing

- Read [style-guide.md](/C:/Users/05507/Documents/Github/AINOTE/docs/style-guide.md).
- Read [quality-bar.md](/C:/Users/05507/Documents/Github/AINOTE/docs/quality-bar.md).
- Read [glossary.md](/C:/Users/05507/Documents/Github/AINOTE/docs/glossary.md) for canonical terms.

## Section Files

- Apply the required frontmatter fields: `id`, `chapter`, `order`, `title`, `status`, `verification`, `page_target`, `keywords`, `source_refs`, `crosslinks`.
- Do not force every section into the same 10-part outline.
- Answer the section question early and explain new terms before using them repeatedly.
- Preserve existing content when syncing from `index.txt`.
- Do not present fabricated personal anecdotes as real experience.
- Prefer natural explanatory prose over checklist-shaped prose.

## Linking

- Use relative Markdown links for manuscript-to-manuscript links.
- Keep source URLs in frontmatter for verification; do not clutter reader-facing prose with source dumps.
